hints: Think of the two partitions as two colors, and require every edge to connect different colors.
Start from every vertex that has not been colored yet, because the graph can contain multiple disconnected components.
During BFS or DFS, assign each uncolored neighbor the opposite color of its current vertex.
If an already-colored neighbor has the same color as the current vertex, an odd-length cycle exists and the graph is not bipartite.
title: Is Graph Bipartite? Problem

notes: The input graph is undirected, so every listed edge appears in both endpoint adjacency lists.
Disconnected graphs are allowed, so every uncolored component must be checked.
constraints: All the values of graph[u] are unique.
If graph[u] contains v, then graph[v] contains u.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: There is no way to partition the nodes into two independent sets such that every edge connects a node in one and a node in the other.
We can partition the nodes into two sets: {0, 2} and {1, 3}.

content.problemStatement:
There is an **undirected** graph with `n` nodes, where each node is numbered between `0` and `n - 1`. You receive a 2D array `graph`, where `graph[u]` is an array of nodes that node `u` is adjacent to. More formally, for each `v` in `graph[u]`, there is an undirected edge between node `u` and node `v`. The graph has the following properties:

* There are no self-edges (`graph[u]` does not contain `u`).
* There are no parallel edges (`graph[u]` does not contain duplicate values).
* If `v` is in `graph[u]`, then `u` is in `graph[v]` (the graph is undirected).
* The graph may not be connected, meaning there may be two nodes `u` and `v` such that there is no path between them.

A graph is **bipartite** if the nodes can be partitioned into two independent sets `A` and `B` such that **every** edge in the graph connects a node in set `A` and a node in set `B`.

Output `true` *exactly when it is **bipartite***.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/10/21/bi2.jpg)

```
Input: graph = [[1,2,3],[0,2],[0,1,3],[0,2]]
Output: false
Explanation: There is no way to partition the nodes into two independent sets such that every edge connects a node in one and a node in the other.
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/10/21/bi1.jpg)

```
Input: graph = [[1,3],[0,2],[1,3],[0,2]]
Output: true
Explanation: We can partition the nodes into two sets: {0, 2} and {1, 3}.
```

**Constraints:**

* `graph.length == n`
* `1 <= n <= 100`
* `0 <= graph[u].length < n`
* `0 <= graph[u][i] <= n - 1`
* `graph[u]` does not contain `u`.
* All the values of `graph[u]` are **unique**.
* If `graph[u]` includes `v`, then `graph[v]` includes `u`.

notes: Reference implementations use iterative graph traversal to avoid recursion-depth concerns.
All hidden tests use only static regular inputs within the documented constraints.
The invariant is that every processed edge connects vertices with opposite colors.
All connected components must be checked because the graph may be disconnected.
solution.approach: Color every connected component with two colors using iterative BFS/DFS. Start each uncolored component with color 0. Every neighbor must receive the opposite color; finding an edge whose endpoints already have the same color proves that the graph is not bipartite.

better.complexity: O((n + m) * alpha(n)) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
better.description: Use Union-Find by forcing all neighbors of each vertex into one group and checking that the vertex itself is not in the same group as any neighbor. With path compression and union by rank, this gives a near-linear alternative.

optimal.complexity: O(n + m) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Traverse every connected component with BFS or DFS and assign alternating colors. When visiting an edge (u, v), color v with the opposite color of u if it is uncolored; otherwise reject immediately when color[u] equals color[v]. The two colors are the two independent sets.

bruteForce.complexity: O(2^n * (n + m)) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Enumerate every possible two-set assignment of the n vertices and check every edge. A valid assignment exists exactly when no edge has equal-colored endpoints.

solution.timeComplexity: O(n + m), where n is the number of vertices and m is the number of undirected edges.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the color array and traversal queue/stack.

followUps: How would you implement the same check using Union-Find?
Why must a disconnected graph start a new traversal from every uncolored vertex?
What changes if edges can be added dynamically and bipartiteness must be maintained?
Could you use DFS instead of BFS, and what changes in auxiliary space?
